Run.question: What is the state of each build of this run? (FR1)
Run.why: A run is the partition: one project per run, kept in full, so what one run did never blurs into another and the main graph holds only results.
Run.alternatives: Runs as nodes in the main graph: rejected, run state is high-volume and short-lived, and the roadmap keeps it apart.

Build.question: Where does each component's build stand, in which group? (FR1, FR2)
Build.why: The unit the plan orders and the loop works on; its state is what the aggregator and the work pack read.

Iteration.question: What happened, pass by pass, with which verdict and gaps? (FR3)
Iteration.why: Kept in full so the run replays: which components needed more than three loops is a query, not a memory.
Iteration.alternatives: Only the last verdict: rejected, the roadmap asks for the whole run.

build_of.question: Which run is this build in? (FR1)
build_of.why: Exactly one run: a build belongs to the run that planned it, and a run is the partition nothing else shares.

iteration_of.question: Which build is this iteration of? (FR3)
iteration_of.why: Exactly one build: an iteration is a pass of one build's loop, and the replay of a build is the walk over its iterations.

follows.question: Which iteration came before this one? (FR3)
follows.why: The order as a fact, not an inference from numbers, so a replay is a walk.
follows.alternatives: The number alone: kept too; the edge makes the chain explicit.
